objectives: Compare PIC platforms (Si, SiN, InP, LN).
Reason about modulators, lasers, filters on chip.
Connect PICs to telecom + datacom + computing.

slides.title: Why photonic integrated circuits matter
slides.body:
**Photonic integrated circuits (PICs)**: integrate many optical functions (laser, modulator, waveguide, filter, detector) on a single chip — analog to electronic ICs.

Motivation:
- **Cost**: high-volume CMOS-like manufacturing.
- **Size**: mm² chips vs benchtop discrete optics.
- **Power**: shorter interconnects + tightly coupled components.
- **Reliability**: no free-space alignment to drift.
- **Performance**: tight integration enables coherent + complex functionalities.

**Platforms** (each with trade-offs):

• **Silicon photonics (SiPh)**: Si waveguides on SOI (silicon-on-insulator) substrate. Mature CMOS-compatible fabs (300 mm). Strong: passives, modulators, detectors (Ge-on-Si). Weak: no on-chip laser (Si is indirect bandgap; lasers via III-V heterogeneous bonding).
- Major players: Intel, Cisco, Marvell (Inphi), Cisco Acacia, AyarLabs, GlobalFoundries, TSMC.
- Applications: data-center 100/400/800/1.6T transceivers; co-packaged optics for switches; sensing.

• **Indium phosphide (InP)**: native laser + active components. Smaller fab base (3-inch typically). Higher cost. Telecom workhorse for active functions.
- Major: Infinera, Lumentum, II-VI (Coherent), Nokia, Furukawa.
- Applications: coherent transceivers, EML modulators, DWDM lasers.

• **Silicon nitride (SiN, Si₃N₄)**: low-loss passive (~0.1 dB/m); CMOS-compatible. Strong: filters, delay lines, microring resonators, gyroscopes, frequency combs (Kerr soliton). No native gain.
- Major: LioniX, Imec, Ligentec, PsiQuantum.

• **Lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) thin-film**: thin-film LN (TFLN) on insulator. Strong electro-optic (Pockels) modulator (>100 GHz BW); χ⁽²⁾ nonlinearities (SHG, OPO).
- Major: HyperLight, Ligentec, Stanford research.

• **III-V on Si heterogeneous**: bond/grow InP-based active devices on Si platform. Best of both worlds.

• **Diamond, SiC, GaN, AlN**: emerging for quantum, UV, high-power.

slides.title: Key PIC components + their integration
slides.body:
**Waveguides** (basic building block):
- SOI: 220-nm-thick Si on 2-µm buried oxide. ~3 dB/cm loss.
- SiN: 200-800 nm strip; ~0.1 dB/cm loss.
- LN: thin-film + ridge; ~0.1 dB/cm loss.
- InP: typical ~0.5 dB/cm.

**Mode converters / spot-size converters**: match fiber mode (~10 µm) to chip mode (~0.5 µm) at edge couplers + grating couplers.

**Modulators**:
- Mach-Zehnder (MZM): split + recombine; differential phase via index modulation. Drives: Si carrier-depletion (~50 GHz), TFLN Pockels (>110 GHz), InP MQW (~50 GHz).
- Electro-absorption modulator (EAM): wavelength-edge absorption shifts under field; InP EML.
- Ring resonator: small (~10 µm) but limited bandwidth; thermal-tuning.

**Lasers (on Si)**:
- III-V/Si heterogeneous bonding: InP DFB or DBR lasers bonded to Si waveguide layer.
- Hybrid integration: III-V chip flip-chip mounted on Si PIC.
- Direct integration: III-V epitaxially grown on Si (research; ongoing improvement).

**Photodetectors**:
- Ge-on-Si: 100% CMOS-compatible; covers 1310 + 1550 nm; ~30-50 GHz bandwidth.
- InP heterogeneous.
- Avalanche + SPAD variants.

**Filters**:
- Mach-Zehnder lattice.
- Microring resonator (high finesse, narrow bandpass).
- Bragg grating (wavelength-selective).
- Arrayed waveguide grating (AWG): wavelength MUX/DEMUX for WDM.

**Switches**:
- Thermo-optic: silicon heater + waveguide; ms-scale switching.
- Electro-optic: faster but more loss.
- MEMS: high cross-talk isolation.

**Couplers**:
- Directional coupler (evanescent).
- Multimode interference (MMI).
- Y-junction.

**Polarization handling**:
- TE/TM modes have different propagation constants.
- Polarization-splitter rotator (PSR) to align polarizations on chip.

slides.title: Co-packaged optics + neural-network accelerators
slides.body:
**Co-packaged optics (CPO)** for switches + servers:
- Switches handling 51.2T-102.4T need optics inside the package (not pluggable transceivers).
- Photons replace copper for chip-to-chip + module-to-module.
- Reduces power 30-50%; enables higher radix switches.
- Cisco + Broadcom + Marvell + Ayar Labs working on CPO for 2025-2027 deployment.

**Optical I/O for AI accelerators**:
- AI workloads bandwidth-bound; copper SerDes hitting limits.
- Optical I/O (OIO): TX/RX optical interfaces co-packaged with compute die.
- Ayar Labs TeraPHY: 8 Tbps/chiplet to NVIDIA + others.
- Lightmatter Passage: dense photonic interposer linking GPUs.
- Celestial AI: photonic memory expansion + GPU-to-GPU links.

**Photonic computing** (more speculative):
- **Photonic neural networks**: matrix-vector multiplication via MZI meshes (Lightmatter, Lightelligence, Luminous, MIT Notion). Promises lower energy/op for inference.
- **Coherent Ising machines**: optical solving of combinatorial problems (NTT, Stanford).
- **Quantum photonic computing**: PsiQuantum + Xanadu + ORCA + Quandela; photonic qubits + linear-optics quantum computing.

**LiDAR + ranging on PIC**:
- FMCW (frequency-modulated CW): coherent ranging via chirped CW laser; less power + better SNR than direct pulsed.
- Integrated chirped-laser + optical phased array + Ge-on-Si detector → all on a chip.
- Aeva, Mobileye, Aurora, Luminar + others using PIC-based lidar for autonomous vehicles.

**Sensing**:
- Gas sensing via mid-IR PIC absorption.
- Biosensing via evanescent-wave ring resonators + microfluidics.
- Inertial sensing via SiN gyroscope (Sagnac effect, on-chip).
- Atomic-clock-on-chip: NIST + JILA + commercial efforts.

**Volumes + cost**:
- 800G pluggable transceiver: ~$1000 (volume).
- Co-packaged optics: $400 / Tbps eventually.
- Lasers + PICs: $1-100/port depending on volume + complexity.
- Cost driven by packaging + test + III-V; Si CMOS volumes promise economies of scale.

question.question: Compare Si vs SiN vs InP PIC platforms for specific applications
question.goal: Choose the right PIC platform for: (a) 800G coherent transceiver; (b) low-loss optical delay line; (c) high-bandwidth quantum-key distribution.

hints: Need: laser (InP) + modulator + detector + DSP electronics.
steps.reveal: **Si + III-V heterogeneous** (or pure **InP**). Si photonics for waveguides + modulators + Ge detectors; III-V laser bonded onto Si chip. Modern 800G ZR + 1.6T pluggables (OSFP, QSFP-DD) use this approach. Pure InP also competitive (Infinera, Lumentum). Si advantage: scale + lower cost; III-V advantage: native gain + better modulator BW at high baud.

steps.prompt: Low-loss optical delay line (km-equivalent in mm scale)?
steps.reveal: **Silicon nitride (SiN, Si₃N₄)**: ultra-low loss (~0.1-1 dB/m); 1 km equivalent achievable in spiral patterns on cm²-size chip. Used: long delay lines for optical computing + lidar; high-Q resonators for filters + Kerr combs + lasers (DBR). Trade-off: no native gain (passive only); no fast modulators (no Pockels in SiN itself; heterogeneous with TFLN or InP).

steps.prompt: High-bandwidth modulator for QKD or coherent telecom (>100 GHz)?
steps.reveal: **Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN)**: leverages LN's strong χ⁽²⁾ Pockels effect for >100 GHz modulator bandwidth at low drive voltage (Vπ ~1-2 V). HyperLight + Ligentec + others. Used: highest-BW coherent transceivers (next-gen >200G/lane); QKD systems requiring fast random-basis switching; integrated frequency combs + quantum-light sources. Si MZ modulators (carrier depletion) ~50 GHz; TFLN doubles+ that.

hints: No single material excels at everything.
steps.reveal: Different platforms have orthogonal strengths: Si for passives + manufacturing scale; InP for lasers + EAMs; SiN for low-loss passives + high-Q; TFLN for modulators + nonlinear. Modern advanced PICs combine multiple platforms via heterogeneous integration: III-V on Si (laser); SiN on Si (filter + comb); TFLN on Si (modulator). Photonic Heterogeneous Integration (PHI) is the frontier. Modern chiplet-style designs assemble best-of-breed photonic + electronic dies into single package.

question.question: Drag to estimate the data-center optical transceiver bandwidth (in Tbps) deployed in 2024 production for AI-cluster interconnect.
question.explanation: 2024 production: 400G + 800G transceivers dominant in AI clusters (NVIDIA Hopper + Blackwell). 1.6T transceivers + co-packaged optics emerging 2025-2027. Pluggable transceivers shipped: ~50M units/year globally. Massive volume: each AI data center ~1M+ transceivers.

question.question: Match each component or technology to its main PIC platform.
question.explanation:
PIC platform specialization:
• **Silicon photonics (SOI)**: 220 nm SOI waveguides, Mach-Zehnder + microring modulators (carrier depletion ~50 GHz), Ge-on-Si detectors (1.3 + 1.55 µm). CMOS-compatible. Lowest cost at volume.
• **InP**: native semiconductor laser (DFB, DBR); EAM (electro-absorption modulator); fast modulator + detector. Cost higher.
• **SiN**: ultra-low-loss passives (~0.1 dB/m); high-Q ring resonators; Kerr-soliton combs; high-Q delay lines + filters. No native gain.
• **TFLN**: strong Pockels effect → fastest modulators (>100 GHz); χ⁽²⁾ for nonlinear conversion (SHG, OPA, comb). Emerging as standard for high-BW coherent + nonlinear applications.

Most advanced PICs use multiple platforms via heterogeneous integration (III-V/Si laser + SiN filter + TFLN modulator on Si carrier).

question.question: Why is co-packaged optics (CPO) being deployed for next-generation network switches + AI accelerators?
options: At 51.2T+ switch bandwidth + 800G+ per port, copper-electrical SerDes hit limits: power, distance, signal integrity. Putting photonic interfaces inside the switch package (not pluggable cages at the front) reduces electrical path length, power per Gbps, + enables higher radix. CPO is being deployed by Cisco + Broadcom + Marvell + Ayar Labs + Lightmatter for 51.2T-102.4T switches + AI accelerator I/O. Reduces interconnect power by 30-50% + enables denser systems.
question.explanation:
**Co-Packaged Optics (CPO)** + the bandwidth crisis:

*Problem at scale*:
Network switches + AI accelerators face exponential bandwidth demand. Current generation:
- 800G per port × 64 ports = 51.2T switch BW.
- Next generation (2025-2027): 1.6T per port × 64 = 102.4T.
- Future: 256-512 ports at multi-Tbps.

Driving issues:
- **SerDes power**: each electrical SerDes lane consumes 5-15 pJ/bit. 51.2T × 8 pJ/bit = ~410 W just for I/O.
- **Reach limit**: PAM4 SerDes at 200+ Gbps/lane lose signal integrity beyond ~10 cm copper trace.
- **Density**: pluggable transceiver cages on front panel limit physical port count + mechanical complexity.

*Pluggable optical transceivers* (current solution):
- QSFP-DD + OSFP cages at switch front panel.
- Plug-in modules host laser + driver + modulator + photodetector + DSP.
- 800G ZR + ZR+ shipped 2022+; 1.6T emerging 2024-2025.
- Drawback: electrical signal still must travel ~10-30 cm of PCB trace from switch ASIC to front-panel module; loss + power.

*Co-packaged optics (CPO)*:
- Photonic chips integrated **inside the switch package** alongside the switch ASIC.
- Direct die-to-die or chiplet attachment.
- Electrical signals stay within ~1 cm of switch ASIC.
- Optical fibers exit the package.

*Power savings*:
- 30-50% reduction vs pluggable for given total bandwidth.
- Lower SerDes power (~3-5 pJ/bit reachable vs 8-15 pJ/bit for pluggable).
- Better thermal management.

*Density*:
- Higher radix possible (>64 ports per switch ASIC).
- More compact systems.

*Reliability challenge*:
- Pluggable: 'hot swap' if defective.
- CPO: defective optic = swap whole module/board.
- Industry solution: highly reliable + redundant designs; longer-term: bank of redundant lanes.

*Industry roll-out*:
- Cisco (Silicon One): CPO products planned 2025.
- Broadcom (Bailly + Tomahawk): CPO 51.2T + 102.4T platforms.
- Marvell (Inphi): CPO photonic engines.
- Ayar Labs (TeraPHY): chiplet-based optical I/O for NVIDIA, Intel, AMD.
- Lightmatter (Passage): photonic interposer for AI accelerators.
- Celestial AI (Photonic Fabric): GPU-to-GPU optical interconnect.

*AI accelerator I/O*:
- NVIDIA H100 + B100/B200: NVLink 4/5 use copper still; future Blackwell+ + Rubin generations may incorporate CPO.
- AMD, Intel, Google TPU, Amazon Trainium: optical I/O roadmap.
- Optical I/O enables larger AI training clusters with more efficient inter-GPU communication.

*Timeline*:
- 2024: pluggable 800G mainstream; CPO demos.
- 2025-2026: first commercial CPO 51.2T deployments.
- 2026-2028: CPO 102.4T + AI accelerator I/O.
- 2030+: integrated photonic-electronic computing increasingly common.

*Larger trend*: photonics is moving from inter-rack (long fiber) to intra-rack (board-to-board) to intra-chip (die-to-die). Each step accelerated by AI workload growth + bandwidth-energy constraints.

hints: Why is copper SerDes hitting limits?
slides.workedSolution: CPO addresses bandwidth crisis at 51.2T-102.4T switches + 800G+/port. Electrical SerDes power (5-15 pJ/bit) + reach (~10 cm copper) limits hit. CPO integrates photonic chips inside switch package alongside ASIC; electrical signals stay <1 cm; 30-50% power savings; higher port density. Industry: Cisco, Broadcom, Marvell, Ayar Labs, Lightmatter, Celestial AI. AI accelerator I/O (NVIDIA NVLink+) also adopting. Timeline: 2025-2027 commercial deployment.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why photonic integrated circuits are following an analogous 'Moore's law' trajectory to electronic ICs, but with different drivers.
question.rubric: Mentions: PIC technology is moving from discrete optics (assembled by hand) to chip-scale + mass-producible. Function counts doubling regularly; per-port cost falling. Drivers different from CMOS Moore's law: not transistor density (photons can't be 5 nm), but: complexity (more components per chip), heterogeneous integration (Si + InP + SiN + TFLN on one carrier), packaging scale (CMOS-fab + chiplet assembly). 2024 state: 800G/1.6T transceivers; co-packaged optics; quantum photonic chips. Drivers: AI bandwidth + data-center power; LIDAR for autonomous driving; quantum computing + networking; sensing + biomedical. Scaling will continue but with engineering creativity (heterogeneous + multi-die + nonlinear) rather than pure feature shrinking. Closes: photonics following CMOS-like trajectory ~20 yr behind, increasingly tightly coupled.
